pr.title: Converge generator checks and fix metadata self-tests and KaTeX
pr.body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Terraform's generator, exact-path verifier and artifact gate used separate implementations from the accepted PowerShell foundation. This PR ports the common implementation from [PS234](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/234), accepted at `98177628b7bc02c646724bfc8aa0fd73fed0cd24`. Terraform retains its language descriptors, independent output allowlist and actual recovery semantic checks.

The generator prepares complete payloads before publication and uses the shared versioned result contracts. The artifact gate retains bounded child execution, checked native status, the first resolved Node executable and final identity checks. The build requires 156 generator assertions twice on each of Windows PowerShell 5.1, Windows PowerShell 7 and native-ext4 Linux PowerShell 7 for the same revision before artifact publication.

Two hosted runs exposed a metadata fixture defect at UTC midnight: synthetic documents kept the previous day's date while child validators read the new day. Private fixture clock controls now cover the actual current, delayed, accepted-worktree, proposed, local and capacity callers. They check exact source anchors and completed clock readbacks, preserve primary errors and remove their state after each action. The production validator and its date policy retain accepted bytes.

Further testing found that literal brackets in a checker path were interpreted as a wildcard by `Set-PSBreakpoint`. The helper now applies `WildcardPattern.Escape` only to its two breakpoint path arguments. Source reading and execution retain the original literal path. The persistent regression uses `clock-probe[fixture].ps1` and the matching decoy `clock-probef.ps1`; it requires exactly two new breakpoints, both on the intended file. Existing negative clock controls and cleanup assertions remain in place.

A fresh audit also identified [GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7) in the Markdown checker dependency graph. An exact workflow-root override selects KaTeX 0.18.2 under `micromark-extension-math@3.1.0`. This crosses the parent's declared range; installation and lint compatibility were checked explicitly. Current callers parse math syntax, and no browser rendering exploit was established here. The dependency-maintenance note records why the override is needed and when to remove it.

## Scope and decisions

The PR changes 16 files: the original 12-file generator port, the SelfTest, two workflow package files and the dependency-maintenance note. The common generator and artifact logic retain only the exact Terraform descriptors and `TerraformRecovery` semantics. CI helpers and build retain repository identity, Terraform's existing `verify` role and output scope. The script index retains the Terraform semantic entry and T1 provenance reference. The four generated documents retain their accepted bytes.

The midnight repair selected C97 after comparing eight options, with correctness across callers and preservation of the production validator weighted highest. The dependency repair selected the exact parent-version override at 96.5/100 after comparing twelve options. The literal-path repair selected B97.5 after comparing ten options: documented escaping preserves the exact checker identity and existing clock controls with a meaningful decoy regression. Scores are engineering judgments; the executed controls provide behavioral evidence.

Round2's Windows-runner concern was refuted by GitHub's supported runner labels and the successful exact-head Windows jobs. The command-length concern was also refuted by measured Windows/Linux limits and actual helper/caller round trips. All three review threads received one disposition and are resolved. The separate literal-path defect is repaired here. Supporting records: [runner decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A03/TF68-R3-windows-runner.md), [transport decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A21/TF68-R4/DECISION.md), [literal-path decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/58aab1903eeb19d3f18fc32ab7359ecde9f45dd5/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A21/TF68-R5/DECISION.md).

## Validation

The final local candidate is `7dd48f52c9e4c17268b4a571919622f4d701e5d0`, tree `0fe10c22e777dba76ce7511def2216bd2ec3b996`, against accepted Terraform base `e21b74fe0b56551008f78f9f2946cd2a0f9c19ce`.

- All 567 Node tests passed with zero failures, cancellations or skips. All 11 repository hooks passed with zero skips, including the complete instruction and mutation self-test. The final guard confirms all 79 source files, Git index/refs/configuration and 1,914 dependency files remained unchanged.
- The local Linux generator suite passed 156 assertions twice. Actual Terraform generation reported NoChange twice and retained all four output hashes. Independent Terraform semantic checks passed.
- Actual repaired path matrices passed 10/10 cases on Windows 7.6.5 and 14/14 on Linux 7.6.3. The original helper failed four and eight cases, respectively, as expected. Each repaired row checks exact breakpoint targets/counts and zero residual clock state. Persistent controls reject the original helper and pass the repair.
- Both platforms passed the actual author fixture with tomorrow's private clock, the actual capacity fixture with yesterday's expected date, and cleanup. Final source/dependency/Git guards passed. The initial reused prior-day scratch driver exited1 because its Oct5 clock preceded valid committed Oct6 metadata; that failed attempt remains preserved and uncredited. The corrected driver changes one checked private author timestamp expression in memory, with checker bytes and real consumers intact.
- Exact helper/caller transport controls passed four positive cases and preserved the intended native parameter refusal on each platform. Maximum measured Windows command: 7,520 characters. Linux argument: 7,272 UTF-8 bytes. Both remain below applicable limits including NUL. Windows parser/analyzer checks report zero errors or warnings.
- The unchanged R2 dependency graph passed 244 affected tests per platform, clean Windows installs and old/patched security controls. Offline Linux tested transported bytes and installed graphs; this does not prove networked Linux installation. The final ordinary two-root audit is CLEAN with no findings or risk exceptions.
- Normal commit hooks and all five actual accepted-base/current-head checks passed: maintenance classification, accepted content, whole-PR author finalization, metadata classification and proposed policy. Independent source/focused review found no material issue and verified the corrected Windows/Linux evidence.

The previous published f89 input passed all 11 ordinary hosted runs, including both 567-test behavior runs, both 11-hook setup runs and both three-platform generator/artifact runs. Those results remain attributed to f89. Fresh current-input remote reviews, hosted checks and independent final native binding remain required. Local Linux does not replace hosted ext4 proof; no new local Windows PowerShell 5.1 execution or recovery-harness acceptance is claimed.

After normal reviewed landing, verify the actual landed workflows. Then carry the common SelfTest, script-index metadata and dependency repairs back to current PowerShell main and compare raw bytes again, retaining only the exact T1/P1 provenance difference. This PR does not complete the paired plan, the recovery harness or its human approval gates. Existing filesystem limitations remain tracked in [PS155](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155).

## Copilot review overview ### 🔵 Needs a closer look It makes large, security-sensitive changes to a privileged CI artifact gate and a three-platform generator-proof trust flow, including a new 488-line harness, warranting final human review despite no defects found. **Review effort:** Balanced **Findings:** None
What changed in this PR This PR ports the shared PowerShell generator/artifact-gate foundation from the accepted PSStyleGuide PR234 into TerraformStyleGuide, keeping Terraform's own language descriptors and state-recovery checks. It restructures `build.yml` into a three-platform generator-proof fan-out (Windows PowerShell 5.1, Windows PowerShell 7, native-ext4 Linux PowerShell 7) whose results must all succeed for the same revision before the privileged `verify` artifact gate runs, and it updates the policy validator, mutation-case catalog, tests, classifier, and script index to recognize these new consumers. **Changes:** - Adds three `generator_*` jobs to `build.yml` plus an `admit-generator-platforms` admission step in `verify`, requiring all platform results (`result == success`, matching `revision`/`GITHUB_SHA`) before artifact publication. - Teaches `Validate-WorkflowPolicy.mjs`/cases/tests about the generator platform jobs, outputs, 23-line proof-step shape, and admission contract, and introduces `Assert-ChildIntegrity` plus a `StyleGuide.*` schema rename in the artifact gate and exact-path verifier. - Adds the new `Test-StyleGuideGenerator.ps1` harness and wires it into the maintenance classifier and `scripts-README.md`. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.github/​workflows/​build.yml` | Adds three platform generator jobs and the aggregate `verify` admission step/needs/outputs. | | `.github/​workflows/​Validate-WorkflowPolicy.mjs` | Adds generator platform/admission/proof validation and the `generatorAdmission` contract constant. | | `.github/​workflows/​Validate-WorkflowPolicy.test.mjs` | Parses the real `build.yml`; asserts 4 verify steps and platform-role mutation categories. | | `.github/​workflows/​workflow-policy-cases.json` | Shifts verify step indices (0→1…3→4) and adds platform/admission mutation cases. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` | Adds `Assert-ChildIntegrity`, two semantic-role branches, and `StyleGuide.GeneratorResult.v2` schema check. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-StyleGuideGenerator.ps1` | New harness exercising generation/publication/identity controls with host + ext4 validation. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-ExactGitPathSet.ps1` | Renames schema to `StyleGuide.ExactGitPathSetResult.v2` and bumps versions. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-CiHelpers.test.mjs` | Adds generator-proof/admission/acquisition and PowerShellExamples role tests. | | `.github/​workflows/​Classify-InstructionMaintenance.mjs` /​ `.test.mjs` | Registers `Test-StyleGuideGenerator.ps1` as a recognized selector. | | `.github/​workflows/​scripts-README.md` | Adds the harness row to the script index. | | `.github/​workflows/​Generate-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` | Emits the renamed `StyleGuide.GeneratorResult.v2` schema consumed by the gate (per PR description). |

review_comments.body: The runner label `windows-2025` is not a commonly available GitHub-hosted runner label (most repos use `windows-latest` or a specific released label like `windows-2022`). If `windows-2025` is not available in the target environment, these jobs will never start. Consider switching to an assured label (or document/enforce the required runner availability in repo policy).

The runner label `windows-2025` is not a commonly available GitHub-hosted runner label (most repos use `windows-latest` or a specific released label like `windows-2022`). If `windows-2025` is not available in the target environment, these jobs will never start. Consider switching to an assured label (or document/enforce the required runner availability in repo policy).

Embedding the full text of `Invoke-AgentInstructionFixtureClock` into a `pwsh -Command` string risks hitting OS/process command-line length limits (and makes failures harder to debug when quoting/escaping changes). A more robust approach is to write the helper function to a temporary `.ps1` file (or reuse an existing fixture helper file) and dot-source it in the child process, then invoke `Invoke-AgentInstructionFixtureClock` normally.

[TF68-R3 decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A03/TF68-R3-windows-runner.md) selects retaining the label and required coverage; the two availability comments share this evidence and need no workflow change.

[TF68-R4 decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A21/TF68-R4/DECISION.md): retain the current transport; no present length or quoting defect reproduced.
Exact unchanged helper/caller probes on Windows 7.6.5 and Linux 7.6.3 measured 7,404 command characters and 7,163 argument bytes, respectively, below the applicable 32,767-character and 131,072-byte limits. Four child controls passed per platform; literal values and the original parameter error survived unchanged.
These probes use a synthetic checker; full fixture coverage comes from the separate successful current-head runs. Future growth requires reassessment. The independently reproduced bracket-path issue is tracked separately as TF68-R5.
